schemaFit.detail: Matches the documented strict subset: objects with additionalProperties:false and all properties required; string enums (the 16-hex ref lists and one-value string enums); anyOf with a standalone {type:'null'} branch, which Groq's recursion example shows. Not documented and so unproven: (1) minimum/maximum on price - absent from the strict subset and used only in best-effort examples, so it may be rejected (400) or ignored; a mechanical rewrite is to drop the keywords and rely on validateDecision for the 0..2 bound; (2) one-value NUMBER enums {type:'number', enum:[3]} - enum is documented, numeric values are not exemplified; (3) the three-level nested anyOf (communication -> proximityUtterance -> referent) - the docs say each branch must follow the subset but give no depth limit; (4) per-call enums of different content with no schema cache - no size or compile limits stated; (5) whether strict:true on /responses is enforced by constrained decoding at all (documented only for Chat Completions). Separately, the request fields background:false and tools:[] are not in Groq's request schema. Needs a live probe before any study call.

Same documented subset and the same five unproven points as gpt-oss-120b on Groq: minimum/maximum, numeric one-value enums, nested anyOf, per-call enums, and strict on /responses. A smaller model also raises the chance that valid-but-wrong choices come out of the constrained enums; that is a quality question, not a schema one.

Listed under strict mode with the same Groq subset, so the same unproven points apply (minimum/maximum, numeric enums, nested anyOf, strict on /responses). Preview status, a 16,384-token output cap and a $4.79 list cost for study 1 (about $9.58 booked at 2x, above the USD 5 allowance) make it a weak candidate despite the schema position.

Schema position is Groq's, if the request is pinned with provider.only=['groq'], allow_fallbacks=false and require_parameters=true; OpenRouter itself says enforcement varies by provider and that strict is passed on only where the provider has a native strict mode. Whether OpenRouter forwards strict and the full keyword set to Groq unchanged is undocumented. The request body we already send (service_tier 'default', store false, background, truncation, text.format json_schema strict) all validates against OpenRouter's Responses request schema. The model ID contains '/' and the provider block is not in the current body.

Not a strict schema path for our transport. Chat Completions accepts only json_object. The Responses text.format json_schema takes name and schema but documents no strict field, no keyword list and no constrained decoding, and ignores unsupported parameters silently. The only documented strict mode is for function tool calls on the /beta base URL, which does not list type null (our nullable anyOf branch) and would need a tool-call transport. effort 'low' also leaves thinking on, which the parser rejects. Fails hard requirement 1 as documented.

Moot: serverless is decommissioned 2026-11-07. For the record, the documented subset covers null, anyOf/allOf/oneOf, additionalProperties and properties; enum, const, minimum and maximum are not listed, and pattern-like constructs that cannot compile are silently relaxed, so enforcement of our enums and the price bound cannot be assumed. service_tier is not a supported Responses field and the model ID contains '/'.

No documented keyword subset and no statement that strict is enforced by constrained decoding; the schema is prepended to the system prompt, which suggests prompt-level guidance plus validation. Chat Completions only, so it also needs a new adapter. Cannot be judged against our nested anyOf, numeric enums or minimum/maximum.
Same as Mistral Small 4: strict flag accepted, enforcement and keywords undocumented, Chat Completions only.

Catalog says structured outputs: Yes and the learn page describes sampler-level constrained decoding, but the API documents no strict flag and no keyword subset, and recommends repeating the schema in the prompt. Chat Completions only. Our anyOf-with-null, numeric enums, nested anyOf and minimum/maximum are all unconfirmed.

JSON Schema mode is not offered for the open-source Qwen series, only JSON Object mode, which 'does not guarantee a specific structure'. The proprietary Qwen3.7/3.8 series that do support it document every keyword we use (null, enum/const, anyOf, minimum/maximum, additionalProperties), but they are not open-weight and are outside this file's scope.

notes: Scope and method: verifier only, hosted open-weight family. No new models, providers or runtimes were searched for and no sub-agents were used. Every cited page was fetched directly on 2026-10-22 (raw markdown where the vendor serves it, otherwise HTML, plus the OpenAPI spec embedded in Groq's API reference and OpenRouter's endpoint/model JSON). The local-runtime items in the task template are not part of this file and were not checked. Scratch copies of the fetched pages are in the session scratchpad, not in the repository. Full result also written to /home/user/The-Node/docs/research/model-options-2026-10-21/verify-open-weight.json.

Material corrections to the research file: (1) Fireworks gpt-oss-120b is being decommissioned from serverless on 2026-11-07 (changelog 2026-10-19), which the file missed; (2) the file's $0.78 Mistral Small 4 cost is $0.85 under its own assumptions; (3) the DeepSeek privacy policy is reachable and does say data may be used for training, scope for API traffic unstated; (4) Alibaba's documented keyword subset does include null, enum/const, anyOf and minimum/maximum, but only for proprietary models, so the exclusion stands; (5) Groq's OpenAPI spec resolves several open items: store:false, truncation and service_tier 'default' are accepted, while background is not in the request schema; (6) Together serverless models are not pinnable (3-day redirect notice).

Survivors are the options whose own API documentation affirmatively promises constrained decoding for a supplied schema AND whose model is still on sale: Groq gpt-oss-120b, gpt-oss-20b and qwen3.8-27b, and OpenRouter-to-Groq as a routing wrapper around the same model. Dropped: Fireworks gpt-oss-120b (serverless removal 2026-11-07); DeepSeek (no documented enforcement on the Responses text.format, unpinnable alias, thinking on by default); Mistral Small 4 and Ministral 8B (enforcement mechanism undocumented, schema is prompt-prepended, Chat Completions only); Together gpt-oss-120b (no strict flag or keyword list, Chat Completions only, redirects rather than pins); Alibaba open-weight Qwen (JSON Object mode only). Mistral and Together are 'unverifiable', not 'refuted': a live probe could promote them, but nothing in their docs does.

Nothing here shows that any survivor accepts our schema. The Groq gaps to probe first: minimum/maximum on price under strict:true; numeric one-value enums; three-level nested anyOf; whether /responses honours strict with constrained decoding or only Chat Completions does; acceptance of background:false and tools:[]/tool_choice:'none'; and compile-time cost of a different schema on every call (no cache hit is possible). Mechanical fallback if minimum/maximum is rejected: drop them and let validateDecision enforce 0..2. No fallback is documented for numeric one-value enums or nested anyOf.

None of the survivors is a drop-in for the current code. Required changes, all in the transport/containment boundary: a configurable endpoint (Groq https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/responses; OpenRouter https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/responses); a model-id check that allows '/' (openai/gpt-oss-120b, qwen/qwen3.8-27b); and a reasoning-item rule. Groq's gpt-oss Responses output always carries a plaintext reasoning_text item (effort cannot be 'none'; the spec has no include_reasoning), and recordedResponse.ts rejects exactly that, so every call would be non-actionable unless the parser is deliberately changed. include_reasoning:false exists on Groq Chat Completions but is not in the Responses schema. For qwen3.8-27b the reasoning default is 'none' only when the request omits reasoning; our effort:'low' turns it on. OpenRouter additionally needs a provider block (only:['groq'], allow_fallbacks:false, require_parameters:true).
